nodes.title: Theorem 10.1(i): regular compatible systems that arise from newforms
nodes.statement: Let (ρ_λ) be an E-rational two-dimensional compatible system of G_ℚ in KW I §5, with every member irreducible and odd, fixed Hodge–Tate numbers a>b, bounded conductor and crystallinity at all sufficiently large coefficient primes. After the Tate twist making the numbers {a−b,0}, there is one normalized characteristic-zero newform f of weight a−b+1≥2 such that every member is the corresponding member of the system attached to f, after common coefficient extension. This is KW I Theorem 10.1(i). The irregular-system theorem 10.1(ii) and the general weight-one descent belong to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.1 and are not inputs here. Corollary 10.2(ii), restricted to finite-image odd Artin representations, is the retained R27.6 export.
hypotheses: The system is regular, not merely of even dimension. Every characteristic-zero member is assumed irreducible; residual irreducibility is a theorem for almost all coefficient primes, not a consequence for each prime.

Use PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.6/residual-members for eventual residual irreducibility, the Fontaine–Laffaille range and a common conductor bound. Its unresolved supplier obligations remain imported.
A Tate twist is normalized in the Hodge–Tate convention of the supplier; the normalized weight is the positive difference plus one. No assertion for general number fields or higher rank is included.
proofSteps: Twist to weights {d,0}, d=a−b>0. Discard the finite exceptional set for residual irreducibility, coefficient ramification, crystallinity and ℓ≤d+1. The residual weight is d+1 and its level divides one fixed conductor bound.

Apply the retained full classical Serre theorem to the remaining residual members. There are finitely many possible levels dividing the bound, characters and normalized newforms of weight d+1, by the modular-forms Hecke theory. Include the finitely many embeddings of their coefficient fields when applying the pigeonhole principle.

One newform and coefficient embedding occurs over infinitely many distinct rational primes. For each fixed good prime r, compare its trace and determinant with the fixed compatible-system polynomial in a common number field. Clear the finitely many denominators of these fixed differences and discard primes dividing them. A nonzero algebraic integer has only finitely many prime divisors, so both differences vanish.
Use same-characteristic Chebotarev–Brauer–Nesbitt recognition separately for every λ to identify that member with the member attached to f. No cross-characteristic isomorphism is asserted.
acceptance: Equal Hodge–Tate weights cannot be substituted: the conclusion would ask for weight one, a different owner.

A level is bounded independently of λ before taking the finite set of newforms; irreducibility of every reduction is not assumed.

nodes.title: Weight-at-least-two witnesses and the solvable-image reduction
nodes.statement: Let p be prime and let ρ̄:G_ℚ→GL₂(F) be S-type over a finite field of characteristic p. Given a characteristic-zero cuspidal weight-one eigenform witness for ρ̄, there is a characteristic-zero cuspidal newform witness of some weight at least two, after a common finite residue-field extension. If p is odd and the residual image is solvable, R17.5 supplies the weight-one witness, so this branch is modular. Thus the remaining qualitative goal is the nonsolvable-image case, proved at R33.4/R33.5 rather than assumed here. Use R15.6’s one modularity predicate; no exact weight or level is asserted by this preliminary implication.
hypotheses: The input is continuous, odd and absolutely irreducible; the weight-shift implication assumes a weight-one witness, whereas the odd solvable-image corollary obtains it from R17.5.
the restriction to k ≥ 2 is a convention justified by the Deligne–Serre congruence, not an omission

Theorem 1.3 is used only for odd p. At p=2 the full solvable branch uses R17.6/qualitative-residual-modularity, followed by this weight shift; the restricted Rohrlich–Tunnell theorem alone is insufficient.

Dickson's classification is cited from its owner, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement, not from the mixed KW I §6 node of R27.1: the modern strand takes from R27.1 only the three good-dihedral declarations (Definition 2.1, Lemma 6.3, Lemma 8.2).

The weight-one witness may have p dividing its level. R15.5/reduction-to-weight-at-least-two-and-to-a-true-eigenform is used directly only in its invertible-level scope. At arbitrary level use its algebraic lifting lemma on the saturated q-expansion-integral analytic lattice described in the proof, using upstream ModularForms coefficient-field and old/new theory. An arbitrary all-cusp sublattice need not preserve the nonzero congruence at infinity; no smooth tame-level Katz base change is asserted.
proofSteps: Normalize the given weight-one newform and multiply by E_n≡1 mod p, with n≥4 even and (p−1)∣n; E₄ suffices at p=2,3. The product h has integral q-expansion, first coefficient 1 and the original good-prime eigenvalues modulo p. For p∤N use the R15.5 application. For p∣N use the analytic application of algebraic eigenvalue lifting (RT p.301): choose a common number field for the finite newform/oldform basis at the new weight, and in that finite-dimensional space take the forms with all q-coefficients in the coefficient DVR. This lattice is finite free because finitely many coefficient maps inject the space into a finite coordinate space; it spans because the basis forms have integral coefficients after one common scaling. The q-expansion formulas make the good Hecke operators and diamonds preserve it. It is saturated in q-expansions, so h is nonzero modulo the uniformizer and its coefficientwise Hecke congruences are actual lattice congruences. Apply R15.5/deligne-serre-eigenvalue-lifting-lemma. This proof-local lattice application imports upstream finite-dimensionality, coefficient-field and old/new theory; no new public lattice definition is planned.

After lifting the good eigensystem, select a simultaneous characteristic-zero eigenvector for the remaining commuting Hecke operators in that eigenspace, normalize it, and use the upstream old/new theorem to obtain a newform of divisor level. No integral bad-prime eigenvalue is prescribed. Recognize its residual representation through the R15.6 interface.

For odd p and solvable residual image import the weight-one witness from R17.5/q-solvable-residual-weight-one and apply the implication. The general qualitative theorem remains the endpoint of R33.4/R33.5.

nodes.title: Modularity transfer along congruences (DP Theorems 1.4–1.7)
nodes.statement: For continuous odd finitely ramified two-dimensional characteristic-zero representations over finite extensions of ℚ_p with de Rham Hodge–Tate weights {0,k−1}, k≥2: (A) if p is odd, two lifts with isomorphic residual representations absolutely irreducible on G_{ℚ(√p*)} are modular simultaneously; (B) if p=2 the corresponding transfer holds for a common nonsolvable residual representation; (C) if p≥5 and the characteristic-zero representation is irreducible with reducible residual semisimplification, it is modular without assuming residual modularity or ordinarity; (D) at p=3 use instead Skinner–Wiles with residual semisimplification 1⊕χ̄₃, a trivial inertia quotient of the characteristic-zero representation, and determinant ψχ₃^{k−1} with ψ finite order. In (D), χ̄₃ is nontrivial on D₃. A modular member identifies every member of its compatible system with the same newform system.
hypotheses: The transfers (A),(B) apply to both lifts with their respective regular weights; no unproved same-component condition is inserted. Residual modularity is discharged by the known modular side.
p*= (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p. The residual restriction criterion is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4, not deduced from global irreducibility alone.

Branch (C) requires characteristic-zero irreducibility and p≥5. At a ramified coefficient prime it uses de Rham regularity; full Weil–Deligne compatibility of a residually reducible almost-strict member is not assumed.

In (D), the unramified ordinary quotient is fixed before choosing which residual character to twist away. The inertia quotient, finite-order determinant factor, and χ̄₃|D₃≠1 are precisely the Skinner–Wiles conditions.
The R32.6 source-independence audit is accepted as a plan with explicit outstanding globalisation obligations. Acceptance of its blueprint is not a completed audit.

nodes.title: Paso 2: application of the prescribed-type lift at the good-dihedral prime
nodes.statement: Let {ρ^{(1)}_ℓ} be the weight-2 system of Paso 1, with coefficient field K and ramification set S₁. Choose a prime q ≡ 1 mod 4, q > 5, larger than every prime of S₁ and split in K. Either ρ^{(1)}_q is modular (solvable residual image: R33.1/solvable-residual-termination, with ρ̄^{(1)}_q not bad dihedral since k = 2 and q > 5), or ρ̄^{(1)}_q : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽_q) — 𝔽_q-valued because q splits in K — has non-solvable image. Choose N ∉ S₁ by Lemma 1.15 (= KW I Lemma 8.2, R27.1): Tr ρ̄^{(1)}_q(Frob_N) = 0 and χ̄_q(Frob_N) = −1, so ρ̄^{(1)}_q|_{D_N} is, up to twist, diag(χ̄_q, 1), and q | N + 1. Theorem 1.9(4) gives a lift ρ^{(2)}_q, crystalline of weight 2 at q, with a specified compatible determinant and actual local solutions, whose inertial type at N is that of τ_N = Ind κ (R33.2/dihedral-local-type-at-n): ρ^{(2)}_q(I_N) is cyclic of order q, acting through κ ⊕ κ^N, and the projective image of D_N is dihedral of order 2q. The image of D_N itself is infinite, since det ρ^{(2)}_q(Frob_N) = ψ(N)·N is not a root of unity; by Theorem 1.4, ρ^{(1)}_q is modular iff ρ^{(2)}_q is, and Theorem 1.11 puts ρ^{(2)}_q in an almost strictly compatible system {ρ^{(2)}_ℓ} with ramification set contained in S₁ ∪ {N}. This is exclusively the Paso 2 application of Theorem 1.9(4), supplied by PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3. The general existence theorem and its cases (1)–(4) are not proved here. Its crystalline clause uses k(ρ̄_q) = 2, inherited from the weight-two Fontaine–Laffaille system at the chosen q.
hypotheses: The local-to-global theorem requires absolute irreducibility over ℚ(ζ_q), compatible determinant and definite local types, and actual local solutions. Nonsolvable residual image supplies the restriction condition.
Lemma 1.15 is stated for 𝔽_q-valued ρ̄, matching the rationality correction to KW I Lemma 8.2; this is why q is taken split in K
the attributions of Theorem 1.9(4) split: partial results in KW I Theorem 5.1, the general case Gee and Snowden Theorem 7.2.1 (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3)
N ≡ 1 mod 8 and N ≡ 1 modulo every prime ≤ q − 1 (Lemma 1.15(2)) are the congruences required by the protected-image argument
The local inertial image at N has order q and the projective decomposition image has order 2q; the full decomposition image of the weight-two arithmetic lift is infinite (E8).

The coefficient prime q lies outside the ramification set S₁ of the weight-two system, so the residual Serre weight is 2, not q + 1. Establish this before invoking the crystalline alternative of Theorem 1.9(4).

Use the local-to-global solvability theorem R24.3/modern-prescribed-type-lifts with actual local lifts, their determinant and definite types. Compatibility of the semisimplified inertia alone does not establish local solvability. At N the selected standard induced lattice matches the full unramified residual D_N representation, after the prescribed unramified twist.
The R33.2 local-type supplier uses coefficients in the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_q containing μ_q. There is no order-q character into ℤ_q×.

For the normalized induced local model the Frobenius determinant is −1. An unramified twist with Frobenius value a has determinant −a² and must satisfy −a²=ψ(N)N, together with the prescribed residual scalar. This may require a finite coefficient extension and is part of the R08.6 local-solution obligation.

Choose N by Lemma 1.15; read off ρ̄^{(1)}_q|_{D_N}.

Apply R24.3/modern-prescribed-type-lifts with the full local lifting problem, crystalline weight two at q and the chosen order-q type at N. The specified local solutions include the determinant. Apply the exact odd transfer, then R24.5/dieulefait-families in its crystalline weight-two input scope to form the system. Its all-member de Rham clause is retained; a bare historical almost-strict predicate is insufficient.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.3: the order-three local type at 2, reached by a congruence at 3
nodes.statement: Let {ρ_ℓ} be an almost strictly compatible system with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, unramified at 3, whose Weil–Deligne representation at 2 is Steinberg up to an unramified twist, and with ρ̄₃ of non-solvable image. Let χ′ be a character of G_{ℚ₄} (ℚ₄ the unramified quadratic extension of ℚ₂) of order 3 and niveau 2, normalised by χ′(Art(2)) = 1, with values in 𝒪 = ℤ₃[ζ], ζ² + ζ + 1 = 0, uniformiser π = ζ − 1, and ρ̃₂ = Ind_{G_{ℚ₄}}^{G_{ℚ₂}} χ′, so ρ̃₂|_{I₂} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′² with trivial monodromy. Then ρ̄₃|_{D₂} ≅ γ ⊗ (χ̄₃ c; 0 1) with γ unramified, and either c = 0 (split case: ρ̄₃ is unramified at 2 and ρ̄₃|_{D₂} ≅ γ ⊗ (η ⊕ 1), η = χ̄₃|_{D₂} the unramified quadratic character) or ρ̄₃|_{I₂} is a nontrivial unipotent module (non-split case). After a finite coefficient extension 𝒪→𝒪′ with residue field k′ containing the input coefficients and γ, there is a stable lattice Λ′ in ρ̃₂⊗Frac(𝒪′) with γ ⊗ (Λ′/𝔪′Λ′) ≅ ρ̄₃|_{D₂}⊗k′. It is obtained by extending one of the following 𝒪-lattices: the standard lattice L₀ = 𝒪e₁ ⊕ 𝒪e₂ of R33.2/dihedral-local-type-at-n in the split case, and the adapted lattice L₁ = 𝒪(e₁ + e₂) ⊕ 𝒪πe₂ in the non-split case; L₀ does not serve in the non-split case. Hence ρ̃₂|_{I₂} is an inertial type compatible with ρ̄₃ at 2 in DP's sense (p. 6), and both reductions have trace 0 at Frobenius. A lift ρ′₃ of ρ̄₃, crystalline of weight 2 at 3, minimal away from 2 and 3, with ρ′₃|_{I₂} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′², exists by Theorem 1.9(4), and also by KW I Theorem 5.1(4) at (p, q) = (3, 2), whose hypotheses ρ̄₃ satisfies; Theorem 1.11 gives a system {ρ′_ℓ} with the same Hodge–Tate weights and ramification set, congruent to {ρ_ℓ} at 3, whose type at 2 comes from an order-3 character. Modularity of one system is equivalent to modularity of the other (Theorem 1.4 at 3).
hypotheses: The input at 2 is Steinberg with an unramified twist, as supplied by the preceding weight-two minimal lift. A ramified twist is not silently discarded.
k(ρ̄₃) = 2: the system is unramified at 3 with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, so ρ₃ is crystalline at 3 and ρ̄₃ is finite flat; this is what allows a crystalline lift at 3
the construction is DP Paso 2's with (q, N) = (3, 2): 3 | 2 + 1

Lattice choice is part of the local lifting problem. The standard lattice reduces to split trivial inertia; the adapted lattice has nontrivial unipotent inertia. Equality of residual traces alone does not identify these modules. The published Lemma 2.3 explicitly removes 2 directly in the unramified branch and uses an integral S₃ representation in the ramified branch; both choices below explain that distinction.

KW I Theorem 5.1(4) at (p, q) = (3, 2): ρ̄₃ is of S-type with k(ρ̄₃) = 2 ∈ [2, p + 1]; ρ̄₃|_{ℚ(µ₃)} is absolutely irreducible, since the image of ρ̄₃ is non-solvable and ℚ(µ₃) is quadratic; ρ̄₃|_{D₂} is (χ̄₃ ∗; 0 1) up to unramified twist; 3 | 2 + 1; χ′|_{I₂} = ω_{2,2} (i = 1, j = 0) has level 2 and order 3; there is no parity condition, as p = 3 is odd. Its conclusion at p is item 2 with k = 2, inertial parameter (1 ⊕ 1, 0), so ρ′₃ is crystalline of weight 2 at 3 and minimal at every ℓ ≠ 2, 3. Its local input at 2 is the level-two inertia-rigid condition of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6/export-away-from-p (b), whose lifts (ρ(F), ρ(σ)) satisfy ρ(F)ρ(σ)ρ(F)⁻¹ = ρ(σ)^q with ρ|_{I₂} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′^q. At (p, q) = (3, 2) the matrices of L₀ and L₁, after an unramified twist, are such lifts of ρ̄₃|_{D₂}. They are not the supplier's own matrices: KW II §3.3.3 writes the lifts of that condition with ρ(F) diagonal

proofSteps: Residual shape at 2. Steinberg up to an unramified twist γ̃ gives ρ₃(Frob₂) the eigenvalues γ̃(Frob₂)·{2, 1}, which reduce to γ(Frob₂)·{−1, 1} because χ̄₃(Frob₂) = 2 = −1 in 𝔽₃; and ρ̄₃(I₂) is unipotent, of order 1 or 3, so wild inertia acts trivially and I₂ acts through its quotient of order 3, generated by the image of a tame generator σ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2). If ρ̄₃(σ) = 1, ρ̄₃(Frob₂) has the distinct eigenvalues ±γ(Frob₂), so ρ̄₃|_{D₂} ≅ γ ⊗ (η ⊕ 1): the split case. Otherwise, in a basis whose first vector spans the inertia invariants, ρ̄₃(σ) = (1 b; 0 1) with b ≠ 0 and ρ̄₃(Frob₂) = (α x; 0 β); the tame relation Frob₂ σ Frob₂⁻¹ = σ² forces α = −β; conjugating by an upper unipotent matrix, which commutes with ρ̄₃(σ), makes ρ̄₃(Frob₂) diagonal, and conjugating by diag(b⁻¹, 1) makes b = 1. So ρ̄₃|_{D₂} ≅ β ⊗ (Frob₂ ↦ diag(−1, 1), σ ↦ (1 1; 0 1)): the non-split case, with one-dimensional inertia invariants.

The standard lattice L₀ (R33.2/dihedral-local-type-at-n at (q, N) = (3, 2)): σ ↦ D₀ = diag(ζ, ζ²) and Frob₂ ↦ F₀ = (0 1; 1 0).
